entries.name: Michael Tabor

expected_cases.charges: New York state Panther 21 conspiracy counts (April 2, 1969 indictment); fled to Algeria in February 1971 during trial.
expected_cases.sentence: Pretrial detention beginning April 2, 1969; released on $50,000 bail in August 1970, as reported in The Black Panther, January 2, 1971, page 2. That report also documents a separate remand on December 29, 1970. The exact later bail-release date remains unverified, but Tabor was free before failing to appear on February 8, 1971. His February 1971 flight is not a prison-release date. Acquitted in absentia May 13, 1971; later exile information is preserved.

expected_cases.charges: Conspiracy to bomb police stations, department stores and the New York Botanical Garden

case.charges: Panther 21 prosecution — separate remand after bail revocation, December 29, 1970
case.sentence: The Black Panther, January 2, 1971, page 2 reports that Tabor was remanded on December 29 after appearing in court with a medical explanation for his absence. This detention follows the August 1970 bail release and must not be joined across that period of freedom. His subsequent release date is unresolved; the March 1971 Bird v. Behagen opinion confirms he was free on bail before his February 8 nonappearance. No exact duration or February 7 release is inferred. Acquitted in absentia May 13, 1971.

entries.rationale: Separate later recommitment; prior interval and profiles preserved. Exact release remains unresolved.

entries.name: Joan Bird

expected_cases.charges: New York state attempted murder (Jan 17, 1969 Harlem police-shootout incident) and Panther 21 conspiracy counts (April 2, 1969 indictment).
expected_cases.sentence: Initially arrested January 17, 1969 in the Harlem incident; earlier custody and bail breaks are not included in this measured interval. This interval covers the Panther 21 detention from April 2, 1969 to July 7, 1970. NYU archives identify photographs of Bird leaving the Women's House of Detention on July 7, corroborating the dated release reported in The Spokeswoman. A Fifth Estate report instead says the fundraising effort paid off July 6; the actual exit date is supported by the photographic record. Bird was remanded again on February 8, 1971, as established by People ex rel. Bird v. Behagen; that later stay is separate. Acquitted May 13, 1971.

case.charges: Panther 21 prosecution — separate remand after bail revocation, February 8, 1971
case.sentence: People ex rel. Bird v. Behagen, decided March 4, 1971, identifies February 8 as the date Bird and Afeni Shakur were remanded after their co-defendants failed to appear. This is a separate stay following Bird's July 1970 bail release. The prosecution ended in acquittal on May 13, 1971; the Johns Hopkins archive identifies a photograph of Bird and Curtis Powell embracing after that verdict. The release endpoint is recorded only as May 1971 pending a direct individual jail-discharge record; no exact day or uninterrupted January 1969-May 1971 total is asserted.

entries.rationale: Separate later recommitment; prior interval and profiles preserved. Exact release remains unresolved.
